subject: Capacity guarantee term and cost-sensitivity for CloudScale deal
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhou <alice@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cloudscale.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Apr 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity guarantee term and cost-sensitivity for CloudScale deal

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the thoughtful conversation yesterday. Per next steps, I attached an updated capacity proposal (cloudscale_capacity_proposal_v3.pdf) and a short draft of a GPU-indexation term that addresses your ask about protecting against unpredictable spot/gpu-market swings (gpu-indexation-term-draft.docx).

TL;DR proposal highlights:
- Reserved pool: 120 A100-equivalent GPUs (mix of A100/H100 compatible slots)
- Commit window options: 12 / 24 / 36 months
- Price sensitivity mechanism: discount tiers tied to a published GPU cost index (monthly published exchange) with a negotiated floor/ceiling so neither side faces unbounded exposure
- Ramp schedule: 30% quarter 1, 60% quarter 2, 100% quarter 3 of committed baseline; burst capacity available for short windows (subject to availability)

Questions for you:
1) Do you prefer a strict fixed-rate discount for the full tenor or a hybrid approach (fixed floor + index-linked top-up/pass-through)?
2) Are your procurement/legal teams comfortable with an index linkage if we hard-cap the pass-through at +8% / -6% relative to the initial committed price?
3) Any constraints on signature authority or internal approvals we should consider for a 24–36 month term?

If you want, I can loop in Finance/Legal to sketch the approval path and a conservative discount band we can pre-authorize for the AE to sign.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
attachments: cloudscale_capacity_proposal_v3.pdf (pdf, 245KB); gpu-indexation-term-draft.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: Alice Zhou <alice@cloudscale.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cloudscale.com>, Mei Chen <mei.chen@globproc.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Capacity guarantee term and cost-sensitivity for CloudScale deal

Rafael —

Appreciate the follow-up and the clear options. A few quick notes from procurement/legal POV:

- We prefer an index-linked approach if it protects us from long-term inflation in GPU prices. Fixed discounts lock us in while the market can move unfavorably.
- That said, our CFO will not accept open-ended upside for the vendor. A symmetric cap is more likely to get through (we'd like +/- 7% around the baseline).
- Signature authority: for anything with term >24 months our CFO signs off; deals under 24 months can be signed by procurement director.
- Ramp: the proposed ramp is fine but we'd like a firm commitment for quarter-by-quarter delivery windows; missed ramps should trigger a credit mechanism rather than immediate termination.

Two asks:
1) Can you share how Redwood intends to define/publish the "GPU cost index" (source, frequency, and whether it's a public benchmark)?
2) Can you provide a simple sensitivity table showing landed per-token cost under baseline, +5%, +10% GPU cost movements for 12/24/36 month tenors?

Cc'd Mei from our procurement team — she'll coordinate legal redlines if we get to an agreed term.

Best,
Alice
Alice Zhou
Sr. Procurement Manager, CloudScale Inc.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhou <alice@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@cloudscale.com>, Mei Chen <mei.chen@globproc.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity guarantee term and cost-sensitivity for CloudScale deal

Alice — thanks, great signal. Looping in Marcus (Finance), Monica (Legal) and Aditya (Head of Sales Strategy) to confirm what we can pre-authorize and how to model the sensitivity.

Marcus / team — quick summary of ask from CloudScale: they want an index-linked pricing safety mechanism with a symmetric cap around baseline (~±7%). They also want missed ramp commitments to trigger credits. Deal is for 120 A100-eq reserved pool with a 24–36 month preferred tenure; procurement requires CFO approval for >24 months.

Proposed internal path (suggested, please confirm):
- We pre-authorize AE-level signature for up to 15% aggregate discount on list for tenors up to 24 months.
- For 24–36 months with index-link and caps beyond the pre-auth band, require VP commercial approval.
- Any indexation clause that allows aggregate vendor-side pass-through >+8% must have explicit finance escalation (CFO review).

Marcus — can you validate the numbers in the sensitivity table below (I produced a conservative first draft attached)? If you can sign off on a pre-authorized band (example: max 15% discount for 24-months with a 6% floor and 8% ceiling on index pass-through) we can surface a clean fig for procurement and speed contract execution.

Suggested sensitivity snapshot (excerpt):
- 12 months: baseline $0.0098/token; +5% GPU cost -> $0.0102/token; +10% -> $0.0110/token
- 24 months: baseline $0.0089/token; +5% -> $0.0093/token; +10% -> $0.0101/token
- 36 months: baseline $0.0081/token; +5% -> $0.0085/token; +10% -> $0.0093/token

Monica — flagging the indexation doc Mei requested. Key legal concerns likely: clarity on index source, auditability, and a short stop-gap that limits retroactive billing changes (we should propose a monthly reconciliation window and a bilateral dispute process).

Next steps: Marcus to confirm permissible discount bands; Monica to propose guardrail language for indexation; Rafael to return an updated sensitivity table and approval grid for CloudScale by EOD.

— Rafael

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity guarantee term and cost-sensitivity for CloudScale deal

Rafael / Aditya —

Reviewed Rafael's draft sensitivity and the proposed control gates. Finance is comfortable with the following, subject to verification of the index source and a monthly reconciliation window:

1) Pre-authorization band: up to 18% off list for term <= 24 months (this gives some AE flexibility and is tighter than your suggested 15%).
2) For deals 24–36 months: require VP Commercial sign-off for >12% discount; any deal that exposes us to a potential >+8% pass-through to customers under the index must have CFO review (we can't accept >+8% vendor-side pass-through without a business case).
3) We need a clear definition of the index: proposed is a composite of published spot GPU hardware market prices (three public exchanges) normalized monthly. Monica will confirm legal language to allow audit and dispute.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
